answer: Sybil resistance follows from bounded random walks over an attestation graph: trust reaching a sybil set must cross its external boundary. A sparse cut with low conductance lets few walks escape within the permitted horizon, so conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds cap the set’s aggregate voting weight by its honest boundary exposure. Thus, a juniper-linked account at the nadir of trust cannot harbor unlimited aliases; their mass remains diluted and detectable.
